topics.flagship-ru-ua: A localized ceasefire reportedly brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump began in a southern Ukrainian city to allow an aid delivery later this week, while Putin spoke with the Norwegian and Finnish leaders. That call was the first contact at this level in more than a year, and Russia and Ukraine are preparing for US-brokered peace talks. A single outlet reports Russian refineries raised throughput by 25% after Ukrainian drone attacks stopped, and CBS photos reportedly show Ukraine's Starlink was throttled during the Oct. 19 Russian strike on a park.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Israeli forces killed at least five people in Gaza, including a 7-year-old girl, bringing the reported toll to 74,555, of whom 1,559 were killed since last year's 'ceasefire'. Polls opened in a tight Israeli general election, with Netanyahu's future at stake. Reports say US forces are ready to strike Iran within 96 hours if ordered, in a US-Israeli conflict now nearly eight months old, and Iranians are bracing for renewed attacks around the elections. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles over Riyadh, and the Houthis claim drone strikes on Saudi border sites.
topics.T15: India is evacuating tens of thousands ahead of 'very severe' Cyclone Arnab, which is due to make landfall Wednesday, with 400,000 people needing evacuation. Other items are about preparedness and recovery: UK government advice to stock up on essentials, a warning about fuel stockholding in Australasia, 1,000+ still sheltered after the July Kumamoto quake, and a Cloudflare review of Q3 2026 internet disruptions.
topics.T01: Jordan acknowledged civilian casualties from its airstrike in Syria against 'Islamic State' targets and expressed regret. Elsewhere, Afghan Taliban shelling reportedly killed one person and injured five in South Waziristan. Shelling in Myanmar's Sittwe killed at least two, drone strikes in Tigray killed seven civilians, India-China border face-offs continue, and a Saudi airstrike reportedly injured three in Taiz. The Intercept reports Pentagon concern over drone threats to bases.
topics.T02: Western governments warn of famine risk in Sudan as war, drought and funding cuts leave millions acutely hungry. The UN Security Council marked 30 years of the children and armed conflict mandate amid record violations. Other items are minor: El Niño crop risks, a solar borehole at a Nigerian IDP camp, and Afghan girls' education.
topics.T03: An Illinois man, Matthew Unglesbee, is accused of mailing letters containing white powder to Congress, marked with his return address. He allegedly told the FBI the substance was salt and that it was a joke.
topics.T04: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly half of those infected dead, making it the country's fastest-growing on record. Regional spillover continues: Nigeria diagnosed a case in a woman with no known Congo travel and flew a patient to Switzerland, Kenya released 20 contacts of its first Bundibugyo case from quarantine, and Uganda imposed 21-day quarantine on returnees from DRC. Separate reports cover a Utah mink-farm bird flu outbreak, dengue in southern Brazil and diphtheria care in Nigeria.
topics.T05: Brazil's opposition party accepted Lula's election win, but Flávio Bolsonaro has not conceded, and his passports were reportedly cancelled. Trump called the vote 'rigged' without evidence. Serbia's student movement won a surprising election victory over Vucic. Netanyahu reportedly claimed the left was 'stealing the election' on Israel's election day. Macron admitted his government was caught off guard by the riots, and reports note US-Myanmar talks.
topics.T06: France's large-scale unrest, framed by the government as riots and by others as student protests over school funding and living costs, remains tense. The government pledged to replace its university admissions platform in 2028 to ease anger. Violent anti-government protests are escalating in Albania, and riots in Sri Lanka reportedly left 30 dead. Most other items are commentary on France.
topics.T07: Two outlets report on France's expansion of its nuclear posture, quoting experts who call it 'extremely destabilizing' and warn that more nuclear weapons raise the risk of accidental use. The coverage is too thin to detail the specific measure.
topics.T08: Jordan struck 'terrorist' positions in Syria after gunmen killed nine people at a funeral in Karak on Friday. Syrian officials reported seven civilians killed, six of them in Daraa. Three Jordanian suspects, injured in a shootout, were arrested, and the interior minister said there was no sign of foreign collaboration. Elsewhere, cattle raids killed at least 72 in South Sudan, three were killed in Kebbi, Nigeria, and two Britons were charged over an alleged terrorist attack at RAF Fairford.
topics.T10: Reports say the Pentagon is preparing bases to survive 90 days without outside support while Britain tells families to stockpile supplies, and the Army is reportedly weighing mass temporary burials at a scale not seen since Korea. Other items cover Germany's next fighter jet choices, UK defense spending questions and India's platform upgrades.
topics.T11: Israel is holding its largest drill in years, practicing for a surprise attack on multiple divisions, with an analyst invoking the 1973 war. South African President Ramaphosa is reviewing a confidential report on Iran's role in a naval exercise. US-Japan forces conducted a coordinated anti-ship strike in Keen Sword 27, and India held exercises with Singapore (SIMBEX) and Indonesia (Garuda Shakti). Oman's 'Sea Lion 2026' is under way, and Hegseth landed in Cebu for regional defense talks.
topics.T12: A ransomware attack claimed by the BYOD group forced UNM Health to cancel surgeries and divert ambulances. North Korea-linked Lazarus is attributed to an espionage campaign (Operation FlashHole) against three South Korean organizations. Other items cover AI-driven cybercrime, Japanese firms compensating users after cyberattacks, and Cloudflare's Q3 outage review.
topics.T13: The EU seeks to give its border agency greater powers, including over deportations. Other reports, from partisan outlets, cover a large Madrid march over migrants in Ceuta, a VOX-PP Senate alliance ahead of Spain's Nov. 29 snap elections, and Irish migration commentary.
topics.T14: France's deputy chief of mission in Tehran was reportedly 'intimidated' this month by people claiming to be Iranian security forces. It is the second incident involving French diplomats in Tehran in under four months, from a single source citing an unnamed source.

bluf: Jordan acknowledged and expressed regret for civilian casualties from its airstrike on 'Islamic State'-linked targets in Syria; Syrian officials reported seven deaths, and the strikes followed a church attack in Karak that killed nine. DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly half of those infected dead, and spread to Nigeria and Kenya; Uganda has imposed 21-day quarantine on returnees from DRC. An Illinois man, Matthew Unglesbee, is accused of mailing white-powder letters to Congress; he allegedly told the FBI it was salt and a joke. A localized ceasefire reportedly brokered by Melania Trump has begun in a southern Ukrainian city to allow aid delivery, as Putin spoke with Norwegian and Finnish leaders, the first call at that level in over a year, ahead of US-brokered peace talks. India is evacuating tens of thousands ahead of 'very severe' Cyclone Arnab, expected to make landfall Wednesday, with 400,000 people needing evacuation. Separately, Israeli voters went to the polls in a tight election, while reports say US forces could strike Iran within 96 hours if ordered, in a conflict nearly eight months old. In Brazil, Flávio Bolsonaro has not conceded Lula's win and his passports were reportedly cancelled.
